clue.text: With children around, coppers get a move on!

indicators.note: around says the word for children wraps round the coins' letter

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring, as in 'the seed of Abraham'
coppers are low-value coins, pennies, abbreviated P

explanation.surface: Police officers, with kids in tow, are told to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' looks like police but means pennies (P), set inside SEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed is to hurry, which is the idiom of getting a move on.

clue.text: It might be as well not to offer resistance

definitions.text: It might be as well not to offer resistance

parts.words: It might be as well not to offer resistance
parts.note: read as a well built of masonry, and also as obstructing by refusing to cooperate

explanation.definitionFit: A wall of masonry, also a verb for obstructive delay; the clue toys with a well made of masonry and with offering resistance.

clue.text: In this context rather more is called for

indicators.note: in this says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: In these circumstances somewhat more is demanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'context rather' reads like ordinary prose; the run of letters spanning the two words is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional amounts are more of something.

clue.text: Gloomy document about news media

indicators.note: about means the document wraps round the media word

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A depressing report about the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or downcast is being gloomy.

clue.text: Offensive front men

parts.note: read as soldiers leading an attack, the forward party of an offensive

explanation.definitionFit: The leading troops of an attack are its spearpoint, the force that goes in first.

clue.text: Little son sustained without sugar

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other pieces surround the small word

parts.note: ten. abbreviates tenuto, the musical direction meaning sustained
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A small boy kept going without any sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but carries its old sense of outside; 'sugar' is the verb, and ten. is the musician's shorthand for tenuto.
explanation.definitionFit: To add sweetness to food is to sugar it.

clue.text: Eradicate mice possibly in one particular area

parts.note: to eradicate is to end or wipe out

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting rid of mice might be possible in one district.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease or species confined to one region is native or local to it.

clue.text: The writer undertook a course of study on the East

indicators.note: on means placed after, in a down clue the second piece follows

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An author studied in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian novelist is a writer.

clue.text: Taking in arms for a pincer movement

definitions.meaning: hugging, arms closing round someone like pincers

explanation.definitionFit: Including means taking in; hugging means wrapping arms round someone, a pincer-like grip.

clue.text: Fearful about Greek leader's lament

indicators.note: about means the word for fearful goes round the letter

parts.note: dire means dreadful, fearful

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Something frightening concerning a Greek chief's mourning song.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral song is a mournful lament.

clue.text: Extended a picnic?

definitions.meaning: a meal laid out in the open air, a spread that is out of doors

explanation.definitionFit: Spread wide means stretched out; a picnic is a meal (a spread) eaten outside.

clue.text: A driver's cautious signal

parts.note: the traffic-light colour warning a motorist to prepare to stop

explanation.definitionFit: The middle traffic light colour, between red and green, warns motorists to take care.

clue.text: Freedom from worry, holding the right to cancel

indicators.note: holding means the first word grips the other piece inside it

parts.note: ease is a state of comfort without anxiety
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Relief from anxiety, with the right to call things off.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub out or delete something is to cancel it.

clue.text: 27, showing ill-humour, scoffed

parts.note: a temper is a fit of bad mood
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed means ate

explanation.surface: Someone sulking and wolfing their food.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is CONTINENT, here the adjective meaning self-restrained, a synonym of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe moderation and self-restraint, especially over food and drink.

clue.text: The craftsman trains a replacement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: replacement says the letters of the two words are put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A craftsman is training up a successor.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker is a craftsman.

clue.text: Name darts-playing 13

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are at play, set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Identify a darts-playing craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is ARTISAN, a skilled worker, as is this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker, such as a plumber, is a craftsman.

clue.text: Fancy the top cereal?

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: Do you like the best breakfast cereal?
explanation.definitionFit: A whim or sudden notion is a fancy.

clue.text: Pop in at length in great distress

parts.note: pop is a word for father, as is pa
fully means at length, completely

explanation.surface: Dad comes in, at last, very upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with agony or acute discomfort means in great distress.

clue.text: Watch a political economist make a bloomer

parts.note: to eye is to watch
John Bright was a 19th-century Radical politician and free-trade campaigner

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on an economist making a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wild flowering plant is a bloomer.

clue.text: Hero worshipper, being poor, retired embarrassed

parts.note: lean means meagre, poor, as in lean years

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for embarrassed is read backwards

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red

explanation.surface: A fan of some idol, hard up, withdrew in shame.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero is a proper name: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: In the legend the young man loved the priestess Hero, so he was literally her worshipper.

clue.text: Note the shop will give refund

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: Be aware the shop will give your money back.
explanation.definitionFit: To give back or repay is to refund.

clue.text: Odd English characters lying on the beach

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the characters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peculiar English people sunbathing at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' links: it is the letters of 'English' that are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rounded pebbles cover many British beaches.

clue.text: Sup rum in class — just think!

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters sit inside the word for class

parts.note: a sect is a group or class

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Drink rum in a classroom, just imagine!
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect is to believe or think something without proof.

clue.text: A fellow getting increases in pay speculates

parts.note: Theo is a man's name, so a fellow
pay rises are increases in wages

explanation.surface: A man who gets salary increases is guessing.
explanation.definitionFit: To form theories is to speculate or conjecture.

clue.text: The jerk is holding on to get a drink

indicators.note: is holding says the twitch word keeps the small word inside it

parts.note: a tic is a twitch, a jerk

explanation.surface: The idiot is clinging on to get a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixer like tonic water is a drink.

clue.text: Spoke repeatedly

parts.note: not talking: the plural of a wheel's spoke, many lines from the centre

explanation.definitionFit: Lines from the hub to the rim of a wheel are spokes; geometric rays from a centre are the plural sense.

clue.text: Just about fifty show natural aptitude

indicators.note: about means the word for just goes round the numeral

parts.note: fair means just, equitable
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Roughly fifty people display a born talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just about' looks like 'nearly', but 'Just' is FAIR and 'about' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift or talent for something is a natural aptitude.

clue.text: A woman can turn in a couple of short articles

indicators.note: in says the turned word goes inside the pair of articles

parts.note: a is a short indefinite article, here twice

indicators.note: turn means the word for can is turned round

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A woman is able to appear in a few brief newspaper pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita is a girl's name, so a woman.

clue.text: Known as a disorderly member? He may well be

definitions.meaning: called, going by the name of

definitions.text: a disorderly member? He may well be
definitions.meaning: the Commons Speaker can formally identify an unruly MP, which leads to suspension

explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' is a Member of Parliament: in the UK House of Commons the Speaker can name an MP for misconduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Called means known as; in Parliament the Speaker 'names' a misbehaving MP, so such a member gets that treatment.

clue.text: Above all, too "economical with the truth"?

parts.note: over means too, as in over-keen
a famous euphemism for telling untruths

explanation.surface: Most of all, a person is far too sparing with the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Economical with the truth' is a well-known British euphemism from a 1986 court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer resting on top of everything lies above all.

clue.text: 12 covers a lot of ground

definitions.meaning: 12 is TEMPERATE: self-restrained, the adjectival sense
a great land mass such as Asia or Africa spreads over a vast area

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means self-restrained, like temperate; the noun is a huge landmass, which indeed spans much ground.

clue.text: Still around as a help in the bakery

indicators.note: around means the word for still encloses the other piece

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not done yet'

explanation.surface: Still around as a helper in the baker's shop.
